summary: Re-review of the six changed blocks (b055, b060, b061, b062, b063, b065) against the English: no fact, negation, speaker, intention, tense or causal link changed and nothing was explained away. The one v1 should_fix (M1, Draco's clipped maxim) is fixed with the wording offered in v1 ('Het is fijn als iemand zijn plaats kent.'); the three optional notes (M2 'Mijn hart smelt', M3 'ongeveer hetzelfde proces', M4 'U \emph{bent} het!') were all applied. All five comprehension questions remain answerable from v2. Three new notes, none requiring action: the presentational 'stond' in b055, the two-sentence form of the b062 aside, and the flat dialogue tag 'antwoordde' that replaced 'lobbed back' at the language reviewer's request.

previous_findings.note: 'Het is goed, zo’n ontmoeting: iemand kent zijn plaats.' → 'Het is fijn als iemand zijn plaats kent.' — one fluent sentence in Draco's affected register, third person, Harry meant but not addressed; this is the first wording offered in v1 (without the 'Aangenaam.' prefix, which the translator declined as a new unglossed lemma). 'to meet' is left to the situation; the sneer survives intact.
'Mijn hart valt flauw.' → 'Mijn hart smelt.' — the flirtatious ring that b064's 'Oeps … als flirten' comments on is back.
'hetzelfde proces' → 'ongeveer hetzelfde proces'; the narrator's hedge of 'a similar process' is restored.
'U bent het \emph{echt}!' → 'U \emph{bent} het!'; stress on the verb as in 'It \emph{is} you!', no added word.

comprehension.q: Why does Harry suddenly start gushing over the pale boy he has only just met?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: He can already predict the rest of the conversation and decides in a half-second of frustration: 'de maat is vol' — he turns the tables and starts fawning himself (b057–b058).

comprehension.q: Is Harry's admiration real? Where does he get his lines — the tears, the handshake — from?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: No, it is an act: he would like tears to come but it does not work, and 'Bij de anderen kwamen de tranen meestal op dit punt' (b060); he asks for the handshake because 'iedereen wilde toch de hand van Harry Potter schudden' (b066). He is imitating his own admirers.

comprehension.q: How does Draco read Harry's behaviour, and what does he believe it tells him about how he will be treated?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: First he is confused ('een beetje in de war'), then a broad smug smile: 'Het is fijn als iemand zijn plaats kent.' (b061). He is pleased with this news: he will get the proper respect for the family Malfidus, and he smiles like the highest king at the least, honest but poor, of his subjects (b065).

comprehension.q: Who else notices what Harry is doing, and how does she react?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: One of the assistants — the one who, it seemed, had recognised Harry earlier — now makes a soft, choked sound (b062).

comprehension.q: Why does Harry think 'Oops' after the line about his heart?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Because 'Mijn hart smelt.' may have sounded a little odd, like flirting with Draco (b063–b064).

findings.fragment: Naast Harry stond een bleke jongen
findings.problem: 'stond' adds a posture the English leaves implicit; the source only says the boy 'seemed to be going through the final stages of a similar process'.
findings.evidence: EN: 'Next to Harry, a pale young boy … seemed to be going through the final stages of a similar process.' vs NL (v2): 'Naast Harry stond een bleke jongen … haar. Hij was, zo leek het, in de laatste fase van ongeveer hetzelfde proces.' (v1 had 'was')
findings.required_fix: None required. In a robe fitting standing is the only reading, and presentational 'stond' is the idiomatic Dutch frame that the split asked for by language L3 needed; the hedge 'zo leek het' and 'ongeveer' are both kept.

findings.fragment: Een van de assistentes herkende Harry eerder al, zo leek het. Ze maakte nu een zacht, \gl{verstikt}{choked} geluid.
findings.problem: The identifying aside ('the one who’d seemed to recognise Harry') has become a narrative statement of its own, so the English single event reads as two statements; 'nu' is added to carry the sequence.
findings.evidence: EN: 'One of the assistants, the one who’d seemed to recognise Harry, made a muffled choking sound.' vs NL (v2) two sentences; v1 had the em-dash aside inside one sentence.
findings.required_fix: None required. Order (identification → sound), hedge ('zo leek het'), anteriority ('eerder al') and the callback to the assistant from the earlier Malkin paragraph all survive; 'nu' adds no information beyond the sequence.

findings.fragment: antwoordde de andere jongen, met een glimlach
findings.problem: 'lobbed back' — the narrator's tennis image, Draco returning Harry's serve in the game of flattery — is flattened to a neutral reporting verb.
findings.evidence: EN: 'the other boy lobbed back, accompanied by a smile such as …' vs NL (v2): 'antwoordde de andere jongen, met een glimlach.' (v1: '\gl{kaatste}{lobbed} de andere jongen terug', replaced on language finding L1, B2 verb)
findings.required_fix: None required; the loss was accepted when the B2 verb was dropped, and the king simile that follows carries the tone. Optional, if a trace of the volley is wanted inside the profile: 'gaf de andere jongen terug, met een glimlach' (teruggeven, A2, in its 'retort' sense).
